# Product Evidence

Two kinds of file live here, and the naming tells them apart.

## `design/UI-APPROVED-0{1,2,3}.{png,md}`

The three product-owner-approved visual references (see
`plans/260802-1037-unified-phase2-ml-llm-gitops/phase-02-build-product-shell-supabase-rbac-and-ux-states.md`,
"Approved UI Baseline"). Immutable baseline — they are never regenerated by a
test run. They set the information hierarchy the implementation must preserve,
not a pixel-perfect target.

## `<route>--<state>--<role>--<project>.{png,json}`

Everything else is a captured frame from the Playwright evidence suites, via
`e2e/evidence-manifest.ts`. **Every frame here is `REFERENCE_FIXTURE` data —
proof the UI renders each state correctly with deterministic fixture data, not
proof of a live runtime.** The manifest JSON says so explicitly
(`dataOrigin: "REFERENCE_FIXTURE"`); tell a fixture-backed frame from a
future executed-runtime frame by that field, not by looking at the image.

Each manifest carries: `route`, `state`, `role`, `viewport`, `project`,
`planeAvailability`, `dataOrigin`, `dataVersion`, `modelVersion`,
`agentVersion`, `sourceSha`, `gitopsSha`, `expected`, `actual`, `redaction`,
`capturedAt`. A PNG exists only for states in the publication allowlist (the
three approved routes at every viewport, plus `degraded`, `forbidden`,
`cost-cap-denied`, `stale-fencing`, `quota-exhausted`, `streaming`) — every
other captured state still gets a manifest, just no committed image, so the
directory does not accumulate a PNG per minor UI variant.

## Regenerating

```bash
cd apps/web
pnpm e2e              # analyst evidence, 3 viewports
pnpm e2e:roles        # platform operator + plane-off evidence
pnpm publish:evidence # copies from e2e/.artifacts/evidence/ into this directory
```

Run `publish:evidence` after each suite — Playwright clears its own output
directory (`e2e/.artifacts/`) at the start of every run, so the second suite
would otherwise wipe the first suite's captures before they are copied out.
`publish:evidence` only ever adds or overwrites files it recognizes; it never
deletes a file it did not write, so this README and the `design/` references
are untouched by every run.

A frame whose `sourceSha` predates a later UI change is stale evidence — the
manifest names the commit each frame was captured against, so a stale frame is
visibly stale rather than silently misleading.

## Accessibility

See `accessibility.md` for the axe pass results, every accepted moderate
violation with its reason, and the keyboard/reduced-motion notes. Regenerate
with `pnpm e2e:a11y` (analyst, plane on) and `pnpm e2e:a11y-roles` (platform
operator, plane off).
